artifacts.summary: 4-phase documentation-and-contract plan adding a categorical point-of-use MUST NOT against forwarding dispatch-row isolation/worktree_path to the Agent tool, strengthening the emitting script's header, and cross-linking the design record.

memory_candidates.content: Contract-placement pattern for orchestration systems: a prohibition that exists only as rationale prose in a design-record/guardrails document is not enforced, because a dispatching lead has no reason to open that file mid-dispatch. The enforceable form is a point-of-use MUST NOT in the section that performs the action, stated categorically over the data shape ('no field of a dispatch row is a tool argument unless this section names it') rather than enumerating the one known offender, with the consequence stated in one clause so the rule is self-justifying where it is read. The motivating instance: a dispatch-row field named identically to a real harness Agent-tool parameter (isolation, enum worktree/remote) makes accidental forwarding syntactically valid and error-free, so no type or schema check catches it. The emitting script's own header must say the field RECORDS a posture already in effect and is never an argument to forward -- descriptive phrasing like 'dispatch-site wiring' reads as a description of what the field configures, not as a statement that it configures nothing downstream.
